title: Choose whether a deadline includes system sleep
goal: Choose an elapsed retry budget or an absolute UTC expiry when deadlines must account for system sleep and civil-clock adjustments.

selectionNotes: Choose an elapsed retry budget or an absolute UTC expiry when deadlines must account for system sleep and civil-clock adjustments.
Older samples are comparisons, not additional catalogue targets.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The primary route uses the net11.0 framework/package asset and .NET 11 behavior.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 consumer with a matching SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical .NET 11 project selects C# 15; the comparison project selects C# 14.

packageAssets: Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref ref/net11.0 and Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime; framework-supplied APIs, no added NuGet package
platforms: Windows desktop/server .NET; physical sleep/resume and hibernation explicitly not tested. No browser/WASI or other-platform execution claim.
prerequisites: Choose whether the policy measures awake elapsed time or an absolute UTC expiry; persist business expiry separately from boot-relative ticks.
constraints: UTC can jump forward/backward; use the documented latch policy and recheck at the point of action.
TickCount64 excludes sleep on Windows starting .NET 11 according to official sources; no physical suspend proof is supplied.
TickCount has a 32-bit wrap period; prefer TickCount64. No timer-resolution or real-time scheduling guarantee.
stabilityLimitations: Stable framework APIs; no experimental opt-in. Actual GA checks establish only the recorded scope.

evidence.scope: Real consumer: UTC past/future checks, ordinary unsignaled OS wait and tick observations; separately deterministic forward/backward clock-jump and expiry-boundary checks. No physical suspend.

humanProof.scope: Pingu approved delivery with this exclusion on 7 November 2026: physical Windows sleep/resume, hibernation, suspended OS-wait outcomes, power-mode effects and suspend interval are not tested. The workstation must not be suspended. Source review and deterministic clocks do not establish suspend execution; no Human handoff or new hardware is required.
